extraction.Name: Leo Hudson
extraction.Cancelled: expressed a desire to have the patent cancelled; the Office ruled in substance that since he actually made an application, favorable consideration could not be given his request for cancellation
extraction.NOTES: Letter from E. E. McKean, superintendent, Rosebud, South Dakota, dated December 11, 1928, to the Commissioner of Indian Affairs, Washington D.C., referencing Circular No. 2464. Hudson is cited as an example case where the Indian made application for fee patent but the application was not forwarded to the Office, possibly due to the 'Declaration of Policy' whereby an Indian of one-half or less Indian blood was issued a patent. At a later date Hudson requested cancellation; investigation found his application in his folder; the Office ruled cancellation could not be favorably considered since he had actually made an application. Document is an administrative cover letter, not a full Circular 2464 report.
